source.name: fn_GetCustomerTotal

assumptions: The dbo schema exists in PostgreSQL (create if needed)
The Orders table exists in the dbo schema with columns CustomerID and TotalAmount
TotalAmount column is numeric type compatible with DECIMAL(18,2)
Function marked as STABLE since it reads from database tables but doesn't modify data
ISNULL converted to COALESCE which is the PostgreSQL equivalent
Parameter prefixed with p_ to follow PostgreSQL naming conventions and avoid conflicts
Local variable prefixed with v_ to follow PostgreSQL naming conventions

reviewFlags.reason: Verify that the function should be STABLE. If Orders table data changes frequently within a transaction and consistent reads are required, confirm this is the correct volatility level.
Ensure the dbo schema and Orders table exist in PostgreSQL. PostgreSQL is case-sensitive with quoted identifiers, so verify schema and table naming conventions.
Confirm that DECIMAL(18,2) precision and scale are sufficient for the business requirements. PostgreSQL DECIMAL is equivalent to NUMERIC.

compatibilityNotes.description: PostgreSQL requires explicit volatility classification (IMMUTABLE/STABLE/VOLATILE). This function is marked STABLE because it reads from tables. SQL Server doesn't have this concept but uses schema binding and determinism hints.
ISNULL converted to COALESCE. Both functions behave identically for this use case, returning 0 when SUM returns NULL.
PostgreSQL schemas work differently than SQL Server. Ensure the dbo schema exists or adjust to use the appropriate schema (public is default).
Added p_ prefix to parameter name following PostgreSQL conventions to avoid potential conflicts with column names in queries.
